test_title: PYST 36: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In poultry farming, what are the primary purposes for developing improved breeds?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Egg and meat production**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poultry farming** is the practice of raising domestic birds such as **chickens**, **ducks**, **turkeys**, and **geese** for the purpose of producing food for human consumption.
 
• The primary commercial and nutritional goal of developing improved breeds in poultry is to maximize the output of **egg and meat production**. These are the two major sources of **animal protein** derived from birds. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Improved breeds are genetically selected to ensure **higher growth rates**, **better egg-laying capacity**, and **resistance to diseases**.
 
• While poultry droppings are used as **manure** (organic fertilizer) because they are rich in **nitrogen** and **phosphorus**, the development of new breeds is never focused solely on manure production. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Products like **wool** are obtained from **sheep** or **rabbits**, and **milk** is obtained from **cattle**, **goats**, or **buffaloes**. These are not outputs of poultry farming. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Breeds developed for **decoration** (ornamental birds) or **sports** (like cockfighting) represent a very small, niche segment and are not the primary purpose of agricultural poultry development. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Broilers:** These are poultry birds raised specifically for **meat production**. They are known for their **fast growth rate** and **high feed conversion ratio**, usually reaching market weight within **6 to 8 weeks**.
 
• **Layers:** These birds are raised specifically for **egg production**. A commercial layer bird starts laying eggs at the age of approximately **20 weeks** and continues for a period of **52 to 72 weeks**.
 
• **Indigenous vs. Exotic Breeds:**
 
 
• **Indigenous breeds** like **Aseel** are known for their hardiness and disease resistance but have lower productivity.
 
• **Exotic breeds** like **Leghorn** (from **Italy**) or **Rhode Island Red** (from **USA**) are used for their high egg-laying capacity.
 
 
 
• **Cross-breeding Objectives:** Breeding programs often cross indigenous and exotic varieties to develop new breeds with traits such as **tolerance to high temperatures**, **low maintenance requirements**, and **reduction in the size of the egg-laying bird** (to consume less feed).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nutritional Requirements:** Poultry feed must be balanced with **proteins**, **carbohydrates**, **fats**, **minerals**, and **vitamins**. Specifically, high levels of **Vitamin A** and **Vitamin K** are maintained in poultry feeds for healthy growth.
 
• **Disease Management:** Poultry birds are susceptible to various diseases caused by **viruses** (e.g., **Ranikhet disease** and **Bird Flu/H5N1**), **bacteria** (e.g., **Salmonellosis**), and **fungi**. Proper **vaccination** and **sanitation** are essential in farming.
 
• **Housing and Shelter:** For optimal production, birds require **well-ventilated** shelters with **controlled temperature** and **clean bedding** (litter) to prevent the spread of infections.
